intro: Google Docs has no native Mac app, so you use it in a browser such as Chrome, Safari or Edge. An AI assistant for Google Docs on Mac works from the screen you already have open. Lazur is a voice assistant for Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about what's on screen. It answers out loud, points at buttons and drafts text at your cursor. Hold fn to dictate.
tldr: Google Docs has no native Mac app. You use it in a browser, so help has to work beside that window.
Lazur explains what's on screen, points at buttons, walks you through features and types drafts at your cursor.
Lazur does not click for you. You do the clicks while it waits and points.
Google's voice typing covers some browsers and English commands. Hold fn for dictation in any app.

blocks.text: People who search this phrase usually want one of three things. They want help while they type in Docs, a faster way to put words on the page, or a way out of a menu they can't find. This page covers all three. It uses real menu paths and shortcuts from Google's own help pages, so you can check each step yourself.
Why Google Docs on Mac is different from a Mac app

Google Docs is a web application. Wikipedia describes it as a browser app, with mobile apps for Android and iOS and a desktop app on ChromeOS. It does not list a native Mac app. So the Mac version is the Docs website in your browser. Docs has no version number you can check on your Mac.

That changes what you need from an assistant. You want a tool that works with the browser window you already have open. You do not want to install a Docs add-on. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, so it works from the window in front of you.
Google Drive for desktop is a different product. It syncs files to your Mac, and it is not the editor. It has its own system requirements, covered below. Mixing the two up causes confusion.
What you can say to Lazur in a Google Doc

Lazur handles five kinds of request while you work in a Doc. It explains what's on screen, points at a control, guides you through a feature, drafts text at your cursor, and dictates what you say. The table shows a sample phrase for each one.

blocks.text: Explain what's on screen in Google Docs

Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a plain question. Lazur looks at the screen while you hold the keys, then answers out loud. Ask about one menu, one sidebar, one banner or one error at a time. Long, mixed questions are harder to answer well.
Here is a real case. You can't remember the Tool finder shortcut. If you forget it, ask Lazur to explain the Tool finder. Google's shortcut page lists ⌥/ for it on Mac, so you can check the answer.
Name the thing you mean. Say 'the highlighted button in the top right' instead of 'this thing'. Lazur can only answer about what is on the screen at that moment, so open the menu or panel first.
Point at a button or menu you can't find
Ask where something is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. You still do the click. Pointing shows you where things sit, so you can find them next time without help.

Try 'Where is word count?' Lazur circles Tools in the menu bar. Then it points at Word count inside that menu. Google's menu path for the same item is Tools > Word count. Open Tools, then click Word count when Lazur points at it.
Pointing needs the item on screen. If a menu is closed, open it first, then ask. Lazur can only point at what it can see.
Walk through a Google Docs feature one step at a time
Guide mode fits tasks with several clicks. Ask Lazur to walk you through the task. It gives one step, then waits. When you click, it gives the next step. You stay in control the whole time.
Guide mode is slower than reading a help article. It is faster than searching for the right panel. Some Docs dialogs show several choices at once, so read each one before you click.
Example: find an older version of a document

items: Say: walk me through version history.
Lazur points at the File menu and waits for you to open it.
Once the menu is open, Lazur points at Version history and names the next item.
Pick a version. Ask Lazur what any label means before you restore a copy.

blocks.text: Google's path for this is File > Version history > See version history. Use the same pattern for any long menu trail. Lazur points, and you click.
Restoring a version is your decision. Lazur points and explains. It does not restore the version for you.
Draft text at your cursor in Google Docs

Ask Lazur to draft text, and it types the draft at your cursor. Short, specific asks work best. 'Draft a short intro for a report on support tickets' gives you something to edit. 'Write the whole report' gives you a block you have to rebuild.
Ask for one section at a time. A Google Doc can hold up to 1.02 million characters, according to Google. That is far more than one request should produce. Short drafts are easier to check.
Read every draft before you keep it. Lazur writes from a short request, so names, dates and numbers in the draft need your check. The document is yours, and so are the facts in it.
Dictate into Google Docs on Mac: voice typing versus Lazur

Google has its own voice typing. Open a document in a supported browser, then click Tools > Voice typing. Click the microphone to speak, and click again to stop. Google's help page says it works with the latest versions of Chrome, Edge and Safari.
Google's page describes only the Tools menu path. It lists no Mac keyboard shortcut. Voice commands work only in English, with the account and document language set to English.

blocks.text: If fn does something else on your Mac, change that in System Settings before you rely on it. Test dictation in a blank Doc first.

If you only need plain speech in one document, Google's tool may be enough. If you dictate into email, notes and Docs, one key in every app is simpler. [Compare the two in more detail](/compare/google-voice-typing-alternative).
Google Docs keyboard shortcuts on Mac

Google's shortcut page is long. Start with a handful. Press ⌘/ in Docs to see the list. The core shortcuts are ⌘C to copy, ⌘V to paste and ⌘B to bold. Ask Lazur to explain any shortcut you don't recognize.

items: ⌘/ shows the common keyboard shortcuts list.
⌘C, ⌘V and ⌘B copy, paste and bold.
⌥/ opens the Tool finder. Google also lists ⌃⌥Z for it.
fn with the arrow keys handles Page Up and Page Down.
fn ⇧ ← extends a selection to the start of a line.

blocks.text: Shortcuts can vary. Google says some may not work for every language or keyboard. Check your keyboard layout if a shortcut does nothing. A small test in a blank Doc is enough.

blocks.title: Test before you rely on it
blocks.text: Google says some shortcuts may not work for all languages or keyboards. Try each one in a blank Doc before you depend on it during a meeting.
Fix Google Docs errors that block your edits

Errors can stop your typing in the middle of a sentence. Google's troubleshooting page covers messages that block edits. Three of its messages are these: 'An error occurred', 'Encountered an error. Please try reloading this page' and 'A server error occurred. Please press Reload in your browser.'
Google lists these steps. Work through them in order.

items: Wait five minutes, then reload the page.
Disable extensions one at a time, in a private window.
Clear your cache and cookies.
Improve your connection.
Update your browser.
If the file keeps failing, make a copy in Drive.

blocks.text: Do not jump straight to clearing cookies. Google's order starts with a wait and a reload, which is the cheapest step.
Lazur can read the error on screen, explain what it means and walk you through each step. It does not fix the file or the browser for you. You do the clicks.
Google Docs file limits: characters and size
A Google Doc can hold up to 1.02 million characters. A text file converted to Google Docs format can be up to 50 MB. Both numbers come from Google's Drive help page.
Characters are the limit to watch. Long reports, pasted tables and large drafts all add up. If you approach the number, split the document into parts, and keep one topic in each part.
Mac, browser and Drive versions you need

Google Docs runs in your browser, so the browser matters most. Google's system requirements page asks for one of the two most recent versions of a supported browser. Cookies and JavaScript must be on. The page names no macOS version for Docs.

Google Drive for desktop is separate. Google's Drive help page lists macOS Ventura 13.0 or higher for it. Release 127.0, dated June 15, 2026, says macOS Monterey 12 is no longer supported, and users must upgrade to continue.
Check the browser first. Then check Drive for desktop, if you use it. One mistake is to blame Docs when the Drive app is the one that needs an upgrade.
Privacy when an AI assistant sees your Google Doc

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.
A Google Doc can hold private material. Before you hold ⌥⌘, close other windows that show client names, passwords or payroll sheets. Lazur sees what is on screen when you ask.
Your company may have its own rules about AI tools. Check them before you use any assistant with confidential files.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Google Docs

items: Expecting it to click. Lazur points and waits. You do the clicks.
Asking while another window is in front. Bring the Doc forward before you hold ⌥⌘.
Asking for a whole report in one request. Ask for one section, then check it.
Trusting a draft without reading it. Names, dates and numbers need your check.
Blaming Docs for a Drive for desktop error. Check which app shows the message.
Using an out-of-date browser for voice typing. Google names the latest Chrome, Edge and Safari.

blocks.text: These mistakes share one root. People treat the assistant as an editor. It is a helper that sits beside the Doc.
What an AI assistant can't do in Google Docs
Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It does not share a document, change permissions or restore a version. Those actions stay with you.
Lazur runs on the Mac only, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. If you use Docs on a Windows PC, this page does not describe a tool you can use yet.
Lazur is a separate app from Google Docs. It is not a plugin or add-in for Docs or any other app. Google's voice typing and Lazur are separate tools with separate jobs.
Your first session with an AI assistant for Google Docs

Open a Doc you already know. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what one menu does. Next, ask Lazur to point at a control you use every day. Then hold fn and dictate one sentence into the Doc. A short test like this shows where the help fits and where it does not.
Lazur has a free trial that needs no credit card. Start from the [download page](/download). When you know which features you use, the [pricing page](/pricing) shows the plans.

faq.question: Is there a Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not a native one. Google Docs runs in a browser and has no version number on your Mac. Google's system requirements page asks for one of the two most recent versions of a supported browser, with cookies and JavaScript on. Google Drive for desktop is a separate app.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Google Docs?
faq.answer: It works with what is on your screen, and a Doc open in your browser is on your screen. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Docs or any other app. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask a question, and hold fn to dictate.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my document for me?
faq.answer: Lazur can draft text and type it at your cursor when you ask. It does not edit files, click buttons or operate other apps for you. You review and keep every change.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my document to AI providers?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your company rules before you use any tool with confidential files.

faq.question: Why doesn't Google's voice typing work in my browser?
faq.answer: Google's voice typing page says it works with the latest versions of Chrome, Edge and Safari. Voice commands work only in English, with the account and document language set to English. Update your browser, then check both language settings.

faq.question: Does Google Docs need the newest version of macOS?
faq.answer: Google's Docs system requirements page names no macOS version. Google Drive for desktop needs macOS Ventura 13.0 or higher. Release 127.0, dated June 15, 2026, says macOS Monterey 12 is no longer supported.

faq.question: How long can a Google Doc be?
faq.answer: Google's Drive help page says a Google Docs document can be up to 1.02 million characters. A text file converted to Google Docs format can be up to 50 MB.

faq.question: Is Lazur available on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a free trial that needs no credit card. It starts when you first open the app. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for plan details after the trial.
